Thanks Maya — this is perfect, very helpful. I ran a quick set of scenarios and have three clear paths we can propose: Hosted (on-demand), Hosted with committed bands, and Dedicated (reserved capacity). Below are concise tradeoffs and a high-level unit-econ estimate; I will follow up with a spreadsheet that breaks it out by model, avg tokens per call, and expected monthly spend.

High level tradeoffs
- Streaming (interactive) vs Batch (background)
  - Streaming: lower tail latency, slightly higher $/1M-token due to reduced batching efficiency. Matches your p95 <=250ms requirement for chat.
  - Batch: much lower $/token for non-interactive workloads; scheduleable nightly windows are ideal for your summaries.

Tier options & indicative unit economics (illustrative)
- Hosted on-demand (no commit): $28/1M tokens (streaming-optimized configuration); good for pilots and unpredictable spikes.
- Hosted committed bands (3–12 month commit): $18–$22/1M tokens depending on volume bands (8–12M/month gets to ~$18–20).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): $12–$16/1M tokens but requires minimum-monthly commit and slotting; best if you need strict p95/p99 guarantees at scale.

How we meet your p95 <=250ms for chat
- Recommend Streaming tier + model routing to low-latency variant. We can also enable 4-bit/8-bit quantization on background variants to reduce cost without affecting chat quality.
- If you need lowest end-to-end latency during spikes, we can include a small reserved burst pool (pay-as-you-burst) in the committed quote.

Preliminary numbers for your band (10M tokens/month example)
- Hosted committed: ~10M * $18/1M = $180/month? (Note: this is illustrative—real quote includes inference tokens + request overhead + persistent KV cache cost).
- Dedicated (small pool): ~$12/1M -> $120/month equivalent + base infra seat.

(clarification: Jonas's note — internal engineering & infra line items typically push effective monthly costs higher; spreadsheet will show full breakdown)

Attachments & links
- I attached the unit-econ worksheet (unit-econ-estimate-jonas.xlsx) with a scenario for 8M / 10M / 12M tokens and the latency configuration assumptions.
- Also shared a short post-demo summary: https://drive.redwood.com/synthesis/post-demo-summary

Next steps
1) Marissa and I will produce two formal quote scenarios (Hosted committed bands + Dedicated small pool) and a short comparison doc by EOD Monday.
2) Schedule a 30-min pricing workshop to walk through the numbers and procurement asks (Maya: you said Tue/Wed after 11am PT — propose Tue 11:30am PT).
3) If procurement wants an initial PO/term sheet, we can produce a redlined SOW and line-item quote after the workshop.

Let me know if you'd like any of the cost math adjusted (e.g., assume 250 tokens per request vs. 400).
